_citation: Leinert, Ch., Bowyer, S., Haikala, L. K., Hanner, M. S., Hauser, M. G., Levasseur-Regourd, A.-Ch., Mann, I., Mattila, K., Reach, W. T., Schlosser, W., Staude, H. J., Toller, G. N., Weiland, J. L., Weinberg, J. L. & Witt, A. N. (1998), 'The 1997 reference of diffuse night sky brightness', Astronomy & Astrophysics Supplement Series 127, 1-99. DOI:10.1051/aas:1998105.
_transcription: Transcribed by hand from the PDF recorded in docs/sources/zodiacal-light.md; page numbers are the journal's. The zodiacal-light maps themselves are in leinert_1998_table16.csv / _table17.csv.

s10_sun._source: Sect. 2, p. 4: 'With V_sun = -26.74 and the mean solid angle of the solar disc ... 1 S10sun = 6.61 10^-12 F_sun/sr'; Table 2, p. 3: 1 S10sun = 1.28e-8 W m^-2 sr^-1 um^-1 at 0.502 um; Table 2 note a: 1 mag-0 star per sr = 3.046 S10.

helios_0.3_1AU.text: I(R)/I(1 AU) = R^(-2.3 +- 0.1) for elongations 16-160 deg (Helios 1/2; Leinert et al. 1980)

colour_fco._source: Sect. 8.4.2, p. 41, Eq. (22): reddening relative to the solar spectrum, colour ratio C(lambda, 500 nm) = f_co, log = log10; f_co = 1 means solar colour. For elongation < 30 deg use the 30 deg relation, > 90 deg the 90 deg relation, interpolate in between. Deviates from 1 by < 20 % from 350 to 800 nm.

pioneer10_poles_table34._source: Table 34, p. 75: brightness of background starlight + integrated starlight at the poles, S10sun units, stars with m_V < 6.5 excluded (adapted from Toller et al. 1987). Pioneer 10 (1978) photometry columns only; the SGP red value is blank in the paper.

pioneer_ipp_star_removal._source: Sect. 10.4, p. 69: 'Individually resolved stars, typically those brighter than 6.5 mag, were removed from the measured brightnesses on the basis of a custom made catalog containing 12457 stars. The absolute calibration was based on the instrument's response to Vega.' Random error 2-3 S10sun, perhaps 5 in the Milky Way and Magellanic clouds (p. 72); spatial resolution ~2 deg.
